editorial.headline: Port Water Transport: The Link Between Quay and Ship
editorial.standfirst: This port-water transport activity connects passengers and cargo between quays, vessels and offshore installations, open nationally to full foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA in Bali.
editorial.body:
Port water transport is the connective work of a harbour: moving passengers or cargo by sea or along the coast where port facilities are not yet fully complete. It uses rede transport to bridge the practical gaps between quay and ship, from a main vessel to another vessel in port waters, or between a quay or vessel and a building or installation at sea. The activity explicitly includes domestic port-water transport for both passengers and goods. Its subject is therefore not open-sea shipping in the abstract, but the short, essential movements that make a working port function.

The activity is open to businesses at every listed scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That range reflects the character of the work itself, which can serve passengers or cargo while connecting the physical points through which port activity takes place. The defining question is not simply whether water moves through a harbour, but how it connects the quay, vessel and installation.

Nationally, the position is direct. The activity is TERBUKA to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In other words, the national record does not place a foreign-equity cap below full ownership for this activity. That clarity matters because the operating scope is precise: it is the transfer function within port waters and between port-side or vessel-side points, for passengers as well as goods.

Bali requires its own reading, but the outcome is not a PMA block. The provincial moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA on an island-wide, permanent basis. This activity is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK in Bali, and the record explains that, at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. It is therefore not blocked by that moratorium. For a foreign investor considering this activity in Bali, the honest picture is that national foreign ownership can reach 100%, while the Bali record places the activity outside the province-wide PMA prohibition because of its stated risk position at the large scale.
